column1: # Game profile of Pokémon: Let's Go, Pikachu! (Switch, base game v0 + update 1.0.2 = v131072). Plays on Android (android.tsv)
# Game Freak's engine on SDK 5.4.151, NVN, Wwise, NEX; subsdk0 is GLSLC (some shaders are compiled at run time), subsdk1 the SDK's movie library (VP9 / Vorbis WebM: the
# opening). Started from the provisional profile the survey wrote (dm/games/profile_guess.py); checked against the dump and the device: the build IDs of the four modules,
# the NPDM's system resource (none) and the heap the game sets ("[mem] heap 3.14 GB (heap region 3.25 GB)")
# 1.0.2 is v131072 (FPSLocker-Warehouse lists build C208DB6A4EF4361F as "v2, 1.0.2", versions in units of 65536)
# every module main imports from: GLSLC (subsdk0) and the movie library (subsdk1)
# The NPDM declares no system resource, so the game has no virtual address memory: main sets a heap of the pool less 64 MB of used memory, 3.14 GB, in the 3.25 GB
# heap region of a 4 GB block (256 MB in front, a 256 MB alias region, a 256 MB stack region). The application pool is the Switch's 3285 MB
# 8,430 shaders from the game files: 8,357 in bin/ (the models' and effects' BNSH, 39 of them compute), 33 in system_resource/, 40 in main. The game also compiles shaders at
# run time with GLSLC that are in no game file: the app captures them on the device and a port with --install adds them to the bundle (docs/ARCHITECTURE.md)
# the rewritten modules are larger than the default 64 MB of used memory
